question: Does density shift male progeny frequency in androdioecy but not under trioecy, and does short-term female decline rule out persistent natural coexistence?

study_2008.cite: Dorken ME & Pannell JR (2008). Density-dependent regulation of the sex ratio in an annual plant. The American Naturalist 171:824-830.
study_2008.source_verified: Original author paper page 826 Table 1 checked both rendered PDF screenshot and text
study_2008.mating_design: Eight paired source populations from Morocco (M1-M5) and Portugal (P1-P3), two independent density arrays per source; progeny grown at common high density to minimize sex-expression plasticity

original_stat_tests.author_tests: low versus high raw sign t=-4.6 p<.005; correcting for parental ratios t=+2.6 p<.05; lambda t=-4.1 p<.005

study_2008.quality_warning: Rendered Table 1 eight low-density offspring cell Ns sum 7293, whereas published total line says 7239 (54 discrepancy). Preserve both; proportions and paired t are computed per-population, not by treating total as verified.

study_2012.cite: Perry LE, Pannell JR & Dorken ME (2012). Two's Company, Three's a Crowd: Experimental Evaluation of the Evolutionary Maintenance of Trioecy in Mercurialis annua (Euphorbiaceae). PLoS ONE 7:e35597.
study_2012.source_verified: Original open full text Table 2 lines 210-251; source text includes original GLMs and discussion
study_2012.counts_per_plot: Table 2 progeny flowers scored after one parent generation; 600 germinated seeds attempted per plot in greenhouse, approx 50% germination; 6076 phenotyped progeny
study_2012.original_interpretation: Presence of females may buffer male siring against density-related hermaphrodite selfing by supplying outcrossable ovules, but female presence itself was NOT independently randomized.
study_2012.contamination_note: Male progeny 0–4% in arrays with no male parents, particularly at low density, indicate inter-plot pollen dispersal despite spatial barriers.
study_2012.morphology_counts_note: Neuter sterile males 0–3% counted as males in original table and GLM.
study_2012.sampling_warning: Plots, not individual offspring, are independent manipulations. Source study contains 10 mixed population ancestries in 20 plots, so plot-wise aggregate not individual fitness.

experimental_male_presence_by_sex_seed_e.metric: Fraction of aboveground biomass allocated to seeds, averaged across density levels; not total individual seed fitness
experimental_male_presence_by_sex_seed_e.original_source: Perry et al. (2012) Results 'Experimental plots', Table 1 male frequency by sex interaction; authors report female +9% without males vs present and hermaphrodite −12% without males vs present
experimental_male_presence_by_sex_seed_e.inference: Male presence was factorially manipulated, females were present in all treatment arms. Sex morph is naturally determined and not randomized, so the sex-morph-dependent seed-effort association is not a within-genotype conversion effect.

study_2024.cite: Nguyen MT, Martignier T & Pannell JR (2024). Widespread male sterility and trioecy in androdioecious Mercurialis annua. American Journal of Botany 111:e16429.
study_2024.genetic_mechanism_inferred: Dominant Y male determination plus cytoplasmic male sterility and multiple partially linked nuclear fertility restorers
genetic_model_assumptions: Restorer fertility cost required but not directly measured
Molecular developmental identity and linkage of restorer alleles not verified
Fit of deterministic predicted morph frequencies does not prove unique mechanism

inferential_limits: 2008 androdioecy and 2012 female-containing trioecy are different source populations, years, densities and genotype histories; observed contrast cannot identify female-presence causal moderation across studies
2008 source Table 1 displays low N=7239 but its eight row progeny Ns sum 7293; do not silently correct original published totals or use contradictory denominator for new p values
2008 source-published proportions rounded to 0.01, paired t from rounded values is a verification check, not a new test from individual pedigree
2012 20 plot-level experimental replicates and 6076 individual offspring; do not count offspring as 6076 independent manipulated experimental units
2012 0–4% male progeny in male-absent plots is evidence of external pollen contamination, not spontaneous sex-detector allele mutation
2012 three morphs are different biological reproductive strategies; male density model differs if females are present but original did not directly randomize their presence
2012 females' higher seed biomass allocation does not equal female genotype increase or long-run stable trioecy
2024 natural 109 populations include categories defined with 2.5% arbitrary cutoff; 36 trioecious populations do not demonstrate indefinite genotype frequency equilibrium
2024 shows no overall female density GLM association despite its male-rich group contrast; do not selectively report the positive group comparison as a universal density effect
2024 CMS and nuclear fertility restoration model is a supported genetic inference, not experimentally verified restorer molecular identity or restorer fitness cost
Source papers by overlapping investigators and source regions are prior art for frequency-dependent evolution, sex-ratio buffering and trioecy; SLK cannot claim first discovery
No original plot-level 2008 full genotype raw CSV, 2012 individual pedigrees or 2024 population supplementary downloads; analysis uses original published table and correctly preserves rounding
No SLK Phi/g0/Delta_R, new mutation probability, rare allele frequency gradient or cross-study causal lifetime fitness are identified

In 2012, male presence×sex morph had a significant interaction on seed-biomass allocation (published F[1,445]=6.3, p<.05), but the original 2012 offspring male-density GLM remained nonsignificant; do not conflate allocation response and next-generation sex-ratio effect.
